channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Como sou democrata, PT é que vai decidir se serei candidato, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that the Workers' Party (PT) will decide in July whether he will be a candidate for re-election in 2026, emphasizing that the decision depends on the 'conjunctural moment'. The remarks were made in an interview with Brazil 247, Diário do Centro do Mundo, and Fórum.

item.title: Lula liga endividamento a bets: 'Lavam dinheiro e assaltam o povo'
item.description: President Lula linked the rise in Brazilian household indebtedness to the growing popularity of online betting (bets), claiming they launder money and exploit the public, particularly in an election year. He reiterated his commitment to shut down betting platforms, citing a study by Ibevar and FIA Business School that identifies online betting as the primary driver of family debt—surpassing credit and interest—and announced plans to improve a debt relief program to complement the 2024 Desenrola initiative.

item.title: Lula diz ter compromisso “moral e cristão” para evitar eleição de Flávio
item.description: Lula states he will run for re-election in 2026 due to a moral, ethical, and Christian commitment to prevent Flávio Bolsonaro’s election, whom he labels a fascist. He criticizes the Bolsonaro government for destroying the country and frames 2026 as the 'year of truth against lies,' citing misleading videos used by the senator. A Datafolha poll shows Flávio at 46% and Lula at 45% in a potential runoff, with both candidates facing high rejection rates.

item.title: Irmão de Bolsonaro posa com deputado pró-Moraes e crítico da anistia
item.description: Renato Bolsonaro, brother of former president Jair Bolsonaro and a pre-candidate for federal deputy, was photographed alongside deputy Antonio Carlos Rodrigues (Republicanos-SP), who left the PL party in 2025 after criticizing Donald Trump and praising Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes. Rodrigues is known for opposing the amnesty bill for those involved in the January 8 attacks and for maintaining close ties with the STF, having served as a key interlocutor for Valdemar Costa Neto in dialogues with Moraes. Renato stated the meeting occurred by chance, as both were staying at the same hotel.

item.title: Lula lidera a disputa contra Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º e 2º turnos, mostra pesquisa
item.description: The CNT/MDA poll shows President Lula (PT) leading the 2026 presidential race in both first and second round scenarios against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). In the first round, Lula has 39.2% compared to Bolsonaro's 30.2%, while in second-round simulations his lead ranges from 4.7 to 16.3 percentage points over tested opponents. The survey interviewed 2,002 people between April 8 and 12, with a 2.2 percentage point margin of error.

item.title: ACM Neto mantém apoio a Caiado
item.description: ACM Neto, pre-candidate for governor of Bahia and vice-president of União Brasil, confirmed his support for Ronaldo Caiado’s presidential candidacy, despite Caiado’s departure from União Brasil to join the PSD. Neto stated that Caiado’s campaign will accommodate multiple parties, reinforcing a strategic alliance between the factions.

item.title: Após Datafolha, Lula critica Faria Lima: "Querem política para taxa de juros deles"
item.description: President Lula criticized São Paulo's financial elite (Faria Lima), claiming they always support candidates opposing social inclusion policies and seek only to protect their own interest rates. The remarks came after a Datafolha poll showed Flávio Bolsonaro leading Lula by one point in a potential second-round matchup (46% to 45%), within the margin of error. Lula also accused Flávio of lying and vowed to combat misinformation firmly.

item.title: "Tem que voltar ao Brasil para cumprir pena", diz Lula sobre Ramagem
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for the return of former Brazilian Intelligence Agency director and federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem to Brazil to serve a 16-year and one-month prison sentence. Lula stated that Ramagem, detained by ICE in the U.S. on Monday (April 13), is a convicted coup plotter and not imprisoned over a minor offense, as claimed by Brazil’s right wing. The remarks were made in an interview with left-leaning outlets on Tuesday (April 14).

item.title: Centrão vai em peso na posse do novo ministro de Lula
item.description: The swearing-in of the new Minister of Institutional Relations, José Guimarães (PT-CE), will be attended by major Centrão leaders, including the heads of União Brasil (Pedro Lucas Fernandes) and PP (Dr. Luizinho), as well as Chamber President Hugo Motta and possibly Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. Guimarães, former government leader in the Chamber, was appointed to replace Gleisi Hoffmann and is seen as a strategic choice to strengthen congressional relations and ensure political coordination for Lula’s government through the end of the year.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tenta minimizar prisão de Ramagem pelo ICE nos Estados Unidos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro downplayed the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem by ICE in the U.S., claiming it is merely an immigration issue and that Ramagem’s asylum request will soon be approved, framing him as another victim of political persecution. However, the Federal Police confirmed the arrest stemmed from international Brazil-U.S. cooperation, as Ramagem is a fugitive from Brazilian justice following a conviction for involvement in a coup plot. The senator used the incident to reinforce his campaign narrative that, if elected in 2026, he will end political imprisonments in Brazil.

item.title: Decisões suspeitas, dinheiro do Master e omissão: o que a CPI aponta contra ministros do STF e PGR
item.description: The final report of the Organized Crime CPI recommends indictment and impeachment proceedings against Supreme Court Ministers Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, Gilmar Mendes, and Attorney General Paulo Gonet for alleged responsibility crimes tied to the Banco Master case. Toffoli is accused of presiding over the case despite a financial relationship with investigated individual Daniel Vorcaro, including private flights and concealment of ties to the Maridt company. The report states his rulings were systematically favorable to Vorcaro and marked by excessive secrecy and conduct incompatible with judicial dignity and decorum.

item.title: Maioria dos brasileiros crê que ministros do STF estão envolvidos com o caso Master, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha survey shows 55% of Brazilians believe Supreme Court ministers are involved in the Master case linked to banker Daniel Vorcaro. Among Flávio Bolsonaro voters, belief rises to 70%, while among Lula voters it is 42%. The findings highlight a crisis of confidence in the STF, with other polls indicating nearly half the population distrusts the country's highest court.

item.title: Leia carta da CNI enviada aos congressistas a favor da escala 6 X 1
item.description: The CNI sent a manifesto to Congress urging rejection of the bill to end the 6x1 work schedule, warning that reducing the workweek to 40 hours while maintaining salaries could raise formal labor costs by up to R$ 267.2 billion annually, increase consumer prices by 6.2%, and disproportionately harm small businesses. The confederation insists changes must involve technical debate, proper transition, and be linked to real productivity gains.

item.title: Crime de responsabilidade do STF “está comprovado”, diz relator da CPI
item.description: The rapporteur of the Organized Crime CPI, Senator Alessandro Vieira, stated that there are elements proving criminal liability involving at least three STF ministers (Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes and Gilmar Mendes) and the Attorney General Paulo Gonet. He announced the indictment of these individuals, emphasizing that the decision is technical and within the Senate’s jurisdiction, despite the commission’s restrictions. The final report, exceeding 200 pages, will be voted on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, with the session postponed from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. for proper review.

item.title: Lula dá entrevista após Datafolha mostrar empate com Flávio no segundo turno: 'Faria Lima sempre vai querer outro candidato'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva gave an interview following a Datafolha poll showing a technical tie in the 2026 presidential runoff, with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) narrowly ahead. Lula stated that 'Faria Lima will always want another candidate,' implying financial market opposition to his candidacy. The article is subscriber-only and underscores the polarization between the PT leader and the Bolsonaro ally.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest mediu o grau de moderação de Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro e Caiado
item.description: The Quaest poll will measure the 'degree of moderation' of Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Caiado, alongside the presidential race temperature and Lula’s approval rating. Set for release tomorrow, the survey includes specific questions on how moderation is perceived among the three leading candidates. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Tarcísio reconduz procurador Paulo Sérgio Costa à chefia do Ministério Público de SP
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas appointed Paulo Sérgio de Oliveira e Costa to a second two-year term as São Paulo's Attorney General after he was reelected by his peers with 1,305 votes against 456 for his opponent. The appointment, published in the Official Gazette, confirms the 2024 selection and follows the governor's constitutional authority to choose any name from the triple list.

item.title: Ao mencionar Ramagem, Flávio fala em 2027 sem “presos políticos”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro stated that former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem, arrested in the U.S. under a Brazilian extradition request related to the January 8 coup plot, will be released soon and that by 2027 Brazil will no longer have political prisoners. He linked Ramagem’s detention to the same narrative that led to Jair Bolsonaro’s conviction, claiming Brazil will return to being a democratic example. Ramagem was sentenced by the STF to 16 years for violent abolition of the democratic rule of law, coup d’état, and criminal organization, and fled to the U.S. before his arrest was ordered.

item.title: Saiba o que acontece se CPI aprovar indiciamento de Moraes, Toffoli, Gilmar e Gonet
item.description: The Parliamentary Inquiry Committee on Organized Crime will decide on Tuesday (14) whether to approve the proposal to indict Supreme Court Justices Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes, along with Prosecutor General Paulo Gonet, over alleged links to Banco Master. The vote is scheduled for 10:18 a.m. and could trigger significant political and institutional repercussions.

item.title: CPI do Crime adia para 14h sessão que votará indiciamento de ministros do STF e PGR
item.description: The Organized Crime Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) postponed to 2 p.m. today (14) the session that will vote on the report by Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE), which proposes the indictment of Supreme Court Justices Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes, as well as Attorney General Paulo Gonet. The postponement follows intense debates over the committee’s legitimacy and potential institutional repercussions.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula reduz diferença para Flávio no 2º turno, indica Apex/Futura
item.description: The Apex/Futura poll released on Tuesday, April 14, shows that President Lula has narrowed the gap with Flávio Bolsonaro by 2.9 percentage points in a hypothetical presidential runoff. In April, the senator led with 48% of voting intentions, but the margin has since tightened. The survey indicates a trend of convergence between the two main contenders for the presidency.

item.title: Indiciamento de ministros do STF proposto pela CPI do Crime precisa de aval de Alcolumbre
item.description: The Organized Crime CPI approved a report calling for the indictment of Supreme Court Justices Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes for responsibility crimes, without criminal characterization. If approved by the CPI majority, the report will be sent to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who will decide whether to bring it to a vote in a special committee. A potential conviction could lead to the impeachment of the justices, though rapporteur Alessandro Vieira did not guarantee consensus for approval.

item.title: Como a imprensa internacional repercutiu a prisão de Alexandre Ramagem pelo ICE nos EUA
item.description: The arrest of Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's intelligence agency and Bolsonaro ally, by ICE in the U.S. received international coverage, with outlets like The Guardian and The Washington Post emphasizing his flight before a 16-year sentence for involvement in the 2022 election coup attempt. The detention, formally linked to immigration violations, was portrayed as the outcome of months-long cooperation between Brazilian and U.S. authorities amid Trump's stricter immigration enforcement.

item.title: Moraes é ministro do STF mais conhecido e Mendonça e Cármen têm a melhor avaliação segundo Datafolha
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes is the most recognized justice with 89% awareness, yet has the worst evaluation among well-known justices. André Mendonça and Cármen Lúcia have the highest approval ratings, while Dias Toffoli records the lowest evaluation score (-16). The Datafolha poll surveyed 2,004 people between April 7-9, 2026, across 137 municipalities, with a two-point margin of error.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Fala de Lula que pôs candidatura à reeleição em dúvida gera interpretações
item.description: Lula stated in an interview that he has not yet decided whether to run for re-election in 2026, sparking speculation among allies and government analysis. Despite public uncertainty, the internal government consensus remains that Lula is a near-certain candidate, with little serious discussion of a backup plan. The statement comes amid challenges including Flávio Bolsonaro's rising poll numbers, struggles to boost popularity, the Iran war, and scandals such as the Master case.

item.title: CPI do Crime Organizado adia para a tarde sessão que vai votar indiciamento de ministros
item.description: The Organized Crime Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) postponed the vote on its final report to 2 p.m., which recommends indicting Attorney General Paulo Gonet and Supreme Court ministers Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, and Gilmar Mendes for crimes of responsibility. Rapporteur Alessandro Vieira stated the focus on these officials is due to the difficulty in obtaining robust evidence for common crimes against figures like banker Daniel Vorcaro, citing resource limitations and institutional barriers.

item.title: Datafolha: 71% dos brasileiros consideram o STF essencial para a democracia
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows 71% of Brazilians view the Supreme Federal Court (STF) as essential to democracy, with strong support among Lula voters (84%), Bolsonaro voters (60%), and blank/null voters (73%). However, 75% believe justices have 'too much power' and that public trust in the institution has declined. André Mendonça leads in approval (+26 points), while six justices, including Alexandre de Moraes and Gilmar Mendes, have negative approval ratings.

item.title: Evento em Brasília promove debates sobre temas como energia, agronegócio e o cenário político
item.description: FCC Government Relations and BMJ consultancy are promoting the 'Conversas do Brasil' event in Brasília this Wednesday (15), featuring panels on energy, agribusiness, connectivity, innovation and the political landscape in an election year. The debate will include representatives from both the governing coalition and opposition to ensure diverse viewpoints. The event starts at 5 PM at Casa Cavo.

item.title: Áudio: Semana Nacional do Esporte vira lei
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.386/2026, establishing the National Sports Week, to be celebrated annually during the week of June 23, National Sports Day. The initiative aims to encourage sports practice as a means to promote health, social inclusion, education, and quality of life across Brazil.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 14 de abril
item.description: JCaesar's April 14, 2026 cartoon satirizes the alleged coup plot involving Jair Bolsonaro, referencing events in Hungary and the tense political climate in Brazil. The critical humor underscores the persistence of destabilizing narratives following the 2022 elections.

item.title: Relatório da CPI do Crime faz enfrentamento político ao STF e recebe críticas no tribunal
item.description: The final report of the Organized Crime CPI voted to indict three Supreme Court justices—Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, and Gilmar Mendes—and the Attorney General Paulo Gonet, alleging they obstructed the commission’s investigations. While relator Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) claims these officials hindered the probe, critics say the report strayed from its original mandate and became a political weapon against the STF. The vote took place on Tuesday (14), the CPI’s last day, amid heightened tensions between Brazil’s Legislative and Judicial branches, with backing from Bolsonaro allies and opposition from government officials and STF ministers.

item.title: 45,6% têm avaliação negativa do Congresso, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Futura/Apex poll released on April 14, 2026 shows that 45.6% of Brazilians rate the National Congress as bad or terrible, with 56.1% disapproving of the work of deputies and senators — the highest disapproval rate among the Three Branches. President Lula’s administration also receives negative evaluations from 43.5% of respondents, while the STF and Executive branch show disapproval rates of 51.9% and 51.4%, respectively. The survey interviewed 2,000 people across 895 cities from April 7–11, 2026, with a 95% confidence level and a 2.2 percentage point margin of error.

item.title: CPI do Crime Organizado pede indiciamento de ministros do STF e sugere intervenção federal no Rio
item.description: The final report of the Senate’s Organized Crime CPI calls for the indictment of Supreme Court Justices Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes, as well as Prosecutor-General Paulo Gonet, for alleged crimes of responsibility and interference in the commission’s investigations. It also recommends that President Lula decree federal intervention in Rio de Janeiro’s public security, citing the advance of organized crime over territories and institutions. The over-200-page document argues that judicial decisions suspending wiretaps and summonses created serious obstacles to the CPI’s work and evidence gathering.

item.title: 55% dos brasileiros acreditam que ministros do STF estão envolvidos no caso Master, diz Datafolha
item.description: 55% of Brazilians believe Supreme Court ministers are involved in the Banco Master scandal, according to a Datafolha poll. The case includes million-dollar contracts with ministers' relatives, message exchanges, and suspicions of illicit fund receipts, leading to 97 impeachment requests in the Senate. The crisis has prompted the STF to consider creating a code of conduct to restore public trust.

item.title: Lula e Motta se reúnem para debater envio de projeto do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: President Lula and House Speaker Hugo Motta are meeting to align on sending a bill to end the 6x1 work schedule, following disagreements over the proposal’s format and timing. The government aims to submit an urgency bill, while the Chamber advances a constitutional amendment (PEC) on the same issue, risking duplication. The meeting seeks to prevent conflict, define leadership, and build a coordinated strategy for legislative processing.

item.title: 'Sem o impeachment de Dilma, Bolsonaro não teria sido presidente', diz Eduardo Cunha
item.description: Former Chamber of Deputies president Eduardo Cunha stated that the impeachment of Dilma Rousseff in 2016, which he led, enabled Jair Bolsonaro's rise to the presidency in 2018. He expressed no regret over the process and plans to leverage this experience to return to Congress in the 2026 elections, noting he receives far more praise than criticism for his role in Dilma's removal.

item.title: Leia a íntegra do relatório da CPI do Crime Organizado
item.description: The final report of the Organized Crime CPI, drafted by Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE), calls for the indictment of Supreme Court Ministers Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes, as well as Attorney General Paulo Gonet. The document will be voted on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, marking the end of the committee's work.

item.title: Após demissão, ex-presidente do INSS compartilha vídeo de ministro da Previdência elogiando queda na fila
item.description: Former INSS president Gilberto Waller Junior was dismissed on Monday after sharing a video of Social Security Minister Wolney Queiroz celebrating a reduction in the benefits backlog. Waller claimed the government had a plan to reduce the backlog since January, but he was replaced by career servant Ana Cristina Viana Silveira amid Palácio do Planalto pressure over the 2.7 million pending requests in March. The firing reflects political concerns about the INSS’s impact on the 2026 elections.

item.title: Gleisi: 'Passadas as eleições, está na hora de pensar em uma reforma do Judiciário'
item.description: Gleisi Hoffmann, PT-PR Senate pre-candidate, argued that judicial reform discussions should begin after the 2024 elections, following the Master Bank case that revealed ties between authorities and banker Daniel Vorcaro. She insisted officials must explain their connections to Vorcaro as a starting point for public debate, tracing the issue’s roots to the Bolsonaro administration, and dismissed 'third-way' candidacies like Ronaldo Caiado’s (PSD) as politically marginal in a highly polarized race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: CPI do Crime: relatório pede indiciamento de Toffoli, Moraes e Gilmar
item.description: The final report of the Organized Crime CPI, presented by Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE), recommends the indictment of Supreme Court Ministers Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, and Gilmar Mendes, along with Prosecutor General Paulo Gonet, over alleged irregularities in investigations. The document criticizes the political and institutional barriers that limited the commission’s ability to investigate high-ranking officials. The report will be voted on this Tuesday (April 14, 2026), concluding the commission’s work.

item.title: Relatório da CPI do Crime Organizado pede a Lula intervenção no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The final report of the Organized Crime CPI, presented by Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE), urges President Lula to decree federal intervention in Rio de Janeiro's public security due to the severity of violence and the state's failure to guarantee basic rights. The report also calls for the indictment of STF ministers Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, and Gilmar Mendes, as well as Attorney General Paulo Gonet, for alleged crimes of responsibility, citing bias, conflicts of interest, and obstruction of investigations. Former Rio governor Cláudio Castro did not attend his scheduled testimony due to health reasons.

item.title: Lula aposta no ‘Desenrola 2.0’ para mudar o rumo da sua campanha
item.description: Lula aims to reverse his high electoral rejection by announcing 'Desenrola 2.0', a new state subsidy program for debt renegotiation targeting 63 million heads of household in federal social programs, with potential discounts of up to 90%. The initiative seeks to improve voter sentiment amid an economic crisis worsened by inflation and record household indebtedness, particularly in revolving credit and overdraft loans. The move comes after polls show that social benefits like Bolsa-Família are now seen as government obligations, not electoral advantages.

item.title: Mais uma promessa que Flávio Bolsonaro não irá cumprir
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro promised that, if elected, he would end the imprisonment, exile, and asylum of individuals for political reasons in Brazil, citing the U.S. ICE arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem as an example. This statement was labeled as another unrealistic pledge, given the legal and migratory complexities involved. The content expresses skepticism about the feasibility of his proposals.

item.title: Nunes Marques assume presidência do TSE em votação simbólica
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques was symbolically elected as the new president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), succeeding Minister Cármen Lúcia, who stepped down early to allow for a transition ahead of the 2026 elections. André Mendonça becomes vice-president, and Dias Toffoli assumes a full seat on the TSE, preserving the court’s structure of three STF ministers, two STJ justices, and two presidential appointees.

item.title: Moraes é o ministro do STF mais conhecido no país, aponta Datalha; veja quais têm melhor avaliação
item.description: Alexandre de Moraes is the most recognized Supreme Court justice in Brazil, known by 89% of the population, followed by Cármen Lúcia (68%) and Gilmar Mendes (62%). Despite lower recognition, André Mendonça received the highest net approval rating (+26 points), while Dias Toffoli had the lowest (-16). The survey also found that 43% of Brazilians distrust the STF, a record high.

item.title: Desaprovação do governo Lula chega a 63,5% no Paraná
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on April 14, 2026, shows 63.5% of voters in Paraná disapprove of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government, with 32.8% approving and 3.7% undecided. Conducted from April 10–12 among 1,500 respondents across 56 municipalities, the poll has a 2.6 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level. The study was funded by the Liberal Party and registered with the TSE under BR-02080/2026.

item.title: O bengalão
item.description: STF ministers see themselves as pillars of democracy and view criticism of the Court as an attack on the regime, especially after the Bolsonaro government, which sought to weaken the Supreme Court to enable a coup. During that period, heterodox interpretations by the justices were incorporated into the legal system and accepted by society as necessary to neutralize the institutional threat.

item.title: Se eleições fossem hoje, Flávio venceria Lula no 1º turno no Paraná
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on April 14, 2026, indicates that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) would defeat Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in the first round of the presidential election in Paraná, with 48.2% voting intention versus Lula’s 25.1%. In a hypothetical second-round scenario, Bolsonaro would lead 58.1% to Lula’s 29.8%. The poll, registered with the TSE under BR-02080/2026, surveyed 1,500 people from April 10–12, 2026, with a margin of error of ±2.6 percentage points and 95% confidence level, and was funded by the Liberal Party.

item.title: O estado onde Flávio Bolsonaro tem vantagem de quase 30 pontos sobre Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads voting intentions in Paraná with 48.2% in the first round and 58.1% in the second round against Lula, who has 25.1% and 29.8%, respectively. The Paraná Pesquisas survey shows 63.5% of Paraná voters disapprove of Lula’s government, reinforcing Bolsonaro’s advantage. Sergio Moro also leads the state race in Paraná.

item.title: Datafolha: 75% afirmam que ministros do STF têm poder demais, e 71% veem Corte essencial para a democracia
item.description: A Datafolha survey shows 75% of Brazilians believe STF ministers have too much power, while 71% see the Court as essential for democracy. Distrust in the STF reached a record 43%, with the highest rejection among Bolsonaro voters (88%), though 64% of Lula voters also perceive excessive power. Despite criticism, a majority still acknowledges the Court’s institutional role in defending democracy.
